CORRECTION FIRST: the figures this dashboard carried as "4 Aug" were actually the 3 Aug closes, one session behind. The real 4 Aug record was S&P 7,736.52 / Dow 54,085.88 — we understated the S&P by 136 points.

Your top risk RALLIED while you were not being told: silver is $62.20 (from ~$58.5 on 4 Aug) and gold $4,270.62, +2.38%, its first open above $4,300 since 17 July — and it rose THROUGH a 5bp yield backup to 4.67%.

The Fed turned hostile: September is now priced ~65% for a HIKE, not a cut. Governor Cook said inflation is "too high" and she is "prepared to act by raising rates"; ISM Services prices hit 70.3 with employment in contraction at 47.4.
The Hormuz de-escalation that drove the 4 Aug record has partly REVERSED — Brent rebounded ~4% on 6 Aug, though WTI is still -11% over three sessions to ~$75 after an Iran-Oman shipping agreement.
DBS delivered: record Q2 profit S$3.08b (+9%), first quarter above S$6b of income, and RAISED FY2026 guidance. Your largest SGX position is outperforming.
Asia split violently: Korea -4.58% with SK Hynix -10.37%, Hang Seng -1.5% (your Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC sleeve), but Shanghai rose. Do not read "Asia" as one exposure right now.

regime.label: Hawkish repricing under record equities
regime.oneLiner: Equities near records and metals rallying, but September is priced for a hike and the oil relief is only half-delivered.

topNews.headline: US equities hit records on 4 Aug — and the dashboard's "4 Aug" figures are actually 3 Aug
topNews.actionable: Correct the stale 4 Aug index line on the dashboard before anything else — it is one full session behind and understates the S&P by 136 points. This was the peak: 7,736.52 on 4 Aug is the record high that the subsequent two sessions have been measured against, so it is the reference level for any drawdown framing on the HK tech and SG bank sleeves.

topNews.headline: 5 Aug mixed: Dow gains to a fresh high while S&P and Nasdaq slip from Tuesday's record
topNews.actionable: The Dow/Nasdaq divergence on 5 Aug is the tell: money rotated out of long-duration tech and into cyclicals/value at a 4.6%+ 10Y. That is the same duration trade that governs his HK/China tech sleeve (0700, 1810, 0981) and favours his SG bank exposure (DBS) over growth. VIX at 15.81 means near-zero fear priced — hedges on the levered silver leg were cheap at this point, ahead of the 6 Aug reversal and Friday's payrolls.

topNews.headline: 6 Aug reversal — Dow sheds 464 points as Brent rebounds nearly 4% and yields move higher
topNews.actionable: This is the single most important development versus the 4 Aug dashboard state: the Hormuz de-escalation that drove the record run is NOT settled, and oil round-tripped a meaningful part of the crash within two sessions. Do not carry "oil crashed, risk-off is over" as the standing narrative. For his book the combination is awkward — higher oil supports the energy sleeve but the accompanying move to a 4.67% 10Y and 5.21% 30Y raises the discount rate on SG REITs (Keppel REIT, Mapletree), the developers (CityDev, UOL, Wing Tai) and the levered silver carry simultaneously.

topNews.headline: ISM Services holds at 54.1 in July but prices jump to 70.3 and employment drops to 47.4
topNews.actionable: This is textbook stagflation-lite: hiring decelerating, services input prices near cycle highs, job-changer wage growth re-accelerating to 7.0%. It is the worst configuration for a levered precious-metals position, because it argues for a Fed that stays restrictive or tightens rather than one that eases. Watch ISM Services Prices at 70.3 as the leading tell for the next core PCE print — a fifth 70+ reading would make a September hike very hard to argue against.

topNews.headline: Challenger job cuts fall to a two-year low in July — 33,429 cuts, AI the top reason for a fifth straight month
topNews.actionable: Counts against the dovish read of the ADP miss. Soft survey-based hiring but firm hard data — claims under 200K and layoffs at a two-year low — means the Fed has no labour-market cover to stop tightening if inflation stays hot. Read as hike-supportive, therefore adverse for the ~1.6x levered silver leg, which is the largest single risk in the book and the most sensitive to both real yields and IBKR margin cost.

topNews.headline: Fed Governor Cook, 5 Aug: "Inflation is too high" and "I am prepared to act by raising rates, if necessary"
topNews.actionable: Note the dependency: one of Cook's three named disinflationary forces is "anticipated oil price declines" — and oil re-rallied nearly 4% the very next session. If Hormuz stays unresolved and crude holds the rebound, a leg of the Fed's own case for patience is removed and the hawkish branch strengthens. Headline PCE at 3.7% is materially worse than the 3.3% core figure the dashboard has been anchoring on; carry both. A governor publicly volunteering hike readiness is a direct risk to the levered silver position.
